newsitem.title: FRANCE: Weather, stocks boosted MATIF wheat trade in April.
newsitem.headline: Weather, stocks boosted MATIF wheat trade in April.

text.p: Concern over world wheat supplies drove French wheat futures trading volume and prices to record highs in April, the MATIF futures exchange said on Monday.

"In the commodities sector, the wheat contract benefited from a favourable environment. Current weather conditions, low stocks and a reduction in sowings in North America and Canada, created market conditions similar to those of the last two years," MATIF said in a statement.
The May contract reached a historical high of 955 francs per tonne on April 14, it said.
Volume was at a record high of 2,712 lots in April, up 137.3 percent over the previous month, MATIF statistics showed.
Average daily volume was 123 lots, with a record 421 lots changing hands on April 7.
Open interest fell 30.1 percent to 1,179 lots at end April over the previous month, after operators sought delivery on 233 positions left outstanding for the now expired May contract.
A total of 121 lots were delivered to the port of Metz and 112 to the port of Frouard, MATIF said.

Concern over the impact on crops of drought in Europe and frost in the U.S., the prospect of low stocks in the European Union and an expected fall in U.S. and Canadian sowings have raised concern over tight supplies and pushed up European Union and world wheat prices.
On April 24 the European Union, eager to protect domestic supplies and keep its prices under control, decided to restore a tax on its daily soft wheat grain exports.
